I made my own sit-stand desk

TL;DR: I made a sit-stand desk from pallets and steel, uploaded the video to YT and got 95K views combined.

Here is Part 1 if you want to watch everything..

And if you want to just skip to the finished product... time indexed link.

I spent about 80 hours on this project, but it was spread over a 4 month time period (8 if you include research and buying parts).

This was also the first project I submitted to YouTube, and for me it has 'blown up' with nearly 80K views on part 2... mind boggling to me. I also try to respond to all questions etc.

Surprisingly, the most expensive portion of the entire project was the epoxy coating. Due to the very three dimensional qualities of the top, there were a lot of sections that were over 1/2" (~13.5mm) deep to fill with epoxy. This came out to more cost than the second most expensive items, the actuators. I should have just purchased a very large bulk container since the epoxy will store indefinitely.

I found that you can have one of two things (power/capacity or speed) and the cost is reasonable. As soon as you want both, the price increases quickly.

Also, a relatively small, 12vdc, high-amperage (10A in this case) switching power supply also isn't cheap.

All-up, I ended up spending a little more than what the amount for which I could have purchased an off-the-shelf sit/stand desk, but the appearance and durability would not have been close to what I ended up with... and... most importantly... I made it. :)

Does anyone else feel as if there has been a swift upturn in a particularly vitriolic and persistent brand of anti-feminist sentiment in recent months? If so, what do you think may have caused it?
Is there a backlash going on for some reason I missed?

It could be that more and more people are attracted in mass to the internet. For reasons like cloud computing, age groups and cell phones, and that means more populations are mixing. The bigger an online space becomes, the more diversity depending on the language and popular topics shared.

I think part of the "vitriolic and persistent brand of anti-feminist sentiment" is due to users crossing paths and feeling the need to engage with the content. Here's an example: from my introduction on [/v/introductions](/v/introductions), "Hi Voat. I'm 23 female, call me puddle. Are there any actual female communities forming here?," I was told "tits or gtfo." For a sub that's recommended for new users, this is the toxicity that's persistent, and the anti-sentiment. is something that's demonstrated on the other end of the spectrum of opinion.

This is also generally because of the populations that have resided longest on social media spaces. Internet communities have a population of 4chan type users that are among those have resided for a long time, that's probably the persistent brand you're thinking of. As newer populations are attracted to and explore similar spaces, both sides will engage, and especially in areas meant to generate discussion.

This all depends on the population of people you're asking. I don't really know the population of this sub, or even this site. Someone might come up with a different answer, I'm just an observer. And if I read your question wrong, I hope my answer at least makes enough sense.
